q: The ratio of principal to 1-year simple interest is 50:1. Find the rate of interest.
The ratio of principal to 5-year simple interest is 10:7. Find the rate.
Shiv borrows money for 5 years; the ratio of principal to total interest is 5:2. Find the ratio of principal to rate.
sol: SI/P=2/5=5R/100 → R=8. Taking P=100 (standard base), P:R=100:8=25:2

q: At 6% SI, in how many years will money:interest ratio become 10:3?
At 8% p.a. SI, in how many years will the interest equal 2/5 of the principal?
SI on a sum is 36% of the principal, and the rate% equals the number of years. Find the rate.
A sum becomes 10× itself at SI. If the time (years) numerically equals the rate, find the rate.
At what SI rate will a sum increase by 30% in 2 years?
A sum doubles in 7 years at SI. In how many years will it become 5×?
sol: SI=P in 7yr (rate=100/7). For 5×: SI=4P → t=28 years

q: In how many years will a sum become 16× itself at 30% SI p.a.?
A sum becomes 7/5× itself in 3 years at SI. Find the rate.
A sum doubles in 15 years at SI. Find the rate.
A sum triples in 4 years at SI. In how many years will it become 5× itself?
sol: SI=2P over 4yrs. For 5×: SI=4P → t=4×4/2=8 years

q: In how many years will a sum double at 15% p.a. SI?
A sum triples at approximately 7.69% p.a. SI. Find the required time.
At what SI rate will a sum become 6× itself in 10 years?
Find the SI rate at which a sum doubles itself in 16⅔ years.
A fixed sum becomes 7× itself in 4 years at SI. In how many years will it become 19× itself?
sol: SI=6P over 4yrs. For 19×: SI=18P → t=18×4/6=12 years
